articles.title: "My Bags Are Getting Searched": FOX's Erin Andrews Pulled Aside by Airport Security After Rams-Eagles Game
articles.summary: Erin Andrews has covered some of the biggest games in the NFL, but getting to her next destination can sometimes be a challenge of its own. After the Los Ang...
articles.body:
Erin Andrews has covered some of the biggest games in the NFL, but getting to her next destination can sometimes be a challenge of its own. After the Los Angeles Rams' Week 4 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, the FOX Sports sideline reporter found herself racing through the airport with her group, only to be held up when security stopped to inspect her belongings.

Andrews shared the chaotic story on Calm Down with Erin and Charissa, the podcast she co-hosts with Charissa Thompson .

"But then I'm the last one because I'm like, 'Everybody go. My bags are getting searched, and we're not just looking for… there's something in their metal.' They're holding up my Invisalign, scanning it. I'm like, 'You guys, it's Invisalign,'" Andrews said on the podcast .

Andrews narrated the story with an urgency reminiscent of the pressure she and her crew were facing at the time. They were already late to reach the airport, having gotten to the car supposed to take them there from the stadium only 15 minutes before boarding. The troupe had already begun thinking of contingency plans, like going to the Newark Airport.

"We got to the airport, and it is boarding before we get through TSA," Andrews added.

Despite the delay, Andrews and her group made it to the flight. By the time they arrived, boarding had reached Zone 6. She celebrated the fact that they had made it, saying, "We made it. They were boarding zone six by the time we made it. Goonies, never say die."

Andrews said she and a travel companion named Dean were racing to make their flight when her bags were held up for a search. She said the "touchless" option was closed at that hour, and the security line still forced them to zigzag through its lanes even though they were the only ones in it.

"We were sprinting," Andrews added. "And I'm maneuvering, you know, the carry-on with the large annoying bag in the middle of it. I even did a little spin. Yeah. I was really proud. I was telling the old gals at Pilates today."

Airports are familiar territory for Andrews, who has described herself on an earlier episode of the same podcast as someone who thrives in travel chaos. Being a sideline reporter, she has to travel to stadiums across the country throughout the season.

"I THRIVE in that situation. In an airport, give me 10 minutes. I can get you a beverage and potentially an appetizer. And you're at the gate ready to board."

Earlier that day, Andrews worked the game from the sideline at Lincoln Financial Field in an all-black rain suit, holding an umbrella while reporting for FOX, and shared the look in an "Instagram vs reality" post on Tuesday.

The Rams rallied from a 20-10 deficit at halftime to beat the Eagles, with Rams running back Kyren Williams scoring two fourth-quarter touchdowns and finishing with 80 rushing yards.

The Rams scored on fourth-quarter drives of 98 and 79 yards, the second capped by Williams' seven-yard TD run with just over a minute left. The win moved Los Angeles to 2-2 and was Rams head coach Sean McVay's first against Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni.

Philadelphia went 0-for-12 on third-down efficiency and failed to score in the second half. The Eagles also lost running back Saquon Barkley to a hamstring injury in the first quarter and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell to a knee injury in the third quarter.

For Andrews, the postgame rush nearly ruined her plans to reach her next stop. But what should have been a straightforward trip through the airport turned into a story worth sharing after the weekend's football was over.

articles.title: Alexi Lalas' Post-World Cup Power Rankings: France Or Spain At The Top?
articles.summary: FOX Soccer analyst Alexi Lalas ranks and explains his top ten soccer squads in the world.
articles.body: This is my first post-World Cup power rankings. I love power rankings and I especially love counter rankings. FIFA has their own rankings (released on Oct. 7), and I'm sure they spend a lot of time and money and technology on the formula to come up with it. I can't say I do the same, it's more of a gut feel. But these are my power rankings, and as I have always said: If you don't like mine, then get your own. 10. Colombia FIFA rank: 11 2026 World Cup Recap: A lot of expectations this summer were put on the Colombians, who were among the trendy dark-horse contenders to win it all. Luis Diaz, who has shined as an attacker for Liverpool and now Bayern Munich, balanced out a tough defense. Nevertheless, a round of 16 loss to an equally stout Switzerland side ended the dream. What's Happened Since: The Colombians had a relatively uneventful window with a win (over Peru), a loss (to Paraguay), and a draw with Mexico (who is ranked No. 10 by FIFA instead) in friendly competition. But Los Cafeteros could make an argument about now being South America's toughest side. Next Opponents: TBD Alexi's Take: "FIFA has Mexico at this spot, but I just think that's ridiculous." 9. Morocco FIFA rank: 6 2026 World Cup Recap: History was made in 2022 as Morocco became the first African nation to reach a men's World Cup semifinals. Leaning on talent that grew up playing in leagues across Europe, Morocco has become a machine. The Atlas Lions lost to France in the quarterfinals (having lost to them in the 2022 semis), but its young core and success at youth tournament levels will keep them around. What's Happened Since: Morocco cruised to two wins in 2027 African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying in September. The drama surrounding the team will be off the pitch as a court ruling this month will decide whether Morocco or Senegal will ultimately be named AFCON champions following the controversial final in 2025. Next Opponents: TBD Alexi's Take: "After making the 2022 World Cup semifinals, we were interested to see whether they could continue that momentum in 2026. Whether it was just a Golden Generation, or it was a moment in time and would be a Croatia-esque storyarc. I think Morocco and this generation of players have proved they are here to stay." 8. Netherlands FIFA rank: 9 2026 World Cup Recap: The team that has historically been among the world's elite (three times runner-up at the men's tournament) provided plenty of entertaining football, backed by one of the best fanbases out there. In the attack, Cody Gakpo and Brian Brobbey shined while the ageless Virgil van Dijk remained the heart-and-soul in defense. A tough loss in the round of 32 against Morocco ended the Oranje's tournament. What's Happened Since: Xavi Hernandez, one of the greatest midfielders in Barcelona history and a 2010 World Cup winner with Spain, was surprisingly picked to be the Netherlands' new manager. Two wins over Serbia and two draws (vs. Germany and Greece) in Nations League action got the Xavi era started on the right foot. Next Opponents: vs. Greece (Nov. 13); vs. Germany (Nov. 16) Alexi's Take: "The Dutch have still never ultimately won the World Cup, but they are still a good solid team. I can be convinced otherwise, but I'm going to give them the benefit of the doubt." 7. Belgium FIFA rank: 8 2026 World Cup Recap: It initially felt like its Golden Generation players of striker Romelu Lukaku, midfielder Kevin De Bruyne, and goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois wouldn't be able to compete at this tournament. But the Red Devils proved people wrong, especially the U.S. men's national team. After a 4-1 beatdown over the USMNT in the round of 16, they would lose to Spain in the quarterfinals. What's Happened Since: Two losses to a more talented France team in the Nations League during this recent window should be tempered by wins over Italy and Türkiye. Those Golden Generation veterans will certainly now give way as talents like winger Jérémy Doku are emerging. Next Opponents: vs. Türkiye (Nov. 12); vs. Italy (Nov. 15) Alexi's Take: "Speaking of good solid teams, we have Belgium next. The U.S. found out in the worst possible way and at the worst possible time how good this team can be." 6. Brazil FIFA rank: 5 2026 World Cup Recap: This team was still one of the biggest draws at the tournament, but the product on the field (led by star winger Vinícius Jr.) never lived up to those mythical yellow jerseys. It's now 24 years since Brazil's last World Cup title. Carlo Ancelotti, one of Europe's greatest club managers at places like Real Madrid and AC Milan, came in to lead a team chock-full of individual talent. Nonetheless, the Seleçao bowed out to Norway in the round of 16. What's Happened Since: Ancelotti remains, Vinicius has had some struggles with his club Real Madrid, and there are still questions about who'll be the next generation's stars. Three wins in friendlies (two against Australia, one against India) aren't going to clarify issues in key areas like defense. Next Opponents: TBD Alexi's Take: "I was high on Brazil, and they did nothing to change that during the World Cup. It's still Brazil, there is still an element of Germany where they are constantly hanging on to the fact." 5. Argentina FIFA rank: 2 2026 World Cup Recap: It was going to be Lionel Messi's Last Dance on the international stage, and Argentina nearly pulled it off. After winning it all in 2022, La Albiceleste reached the final in the summer but was dominated by Spain in a tough 1-0 loss. Even at age 39, Messi was the focal point and the inspirational guiding light for a talented team. He finished with 8 goals, behind only France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race. What's Happened Since: Messi officially bid adios to playing for Argentina in a send-off match against African team Benin. It was an emotional night on Oct. 6 in Buenos Aires as a whole nation honored one of sport's greatest figures. The era changes, but the talent will still be there with youngsters like Julian Alvarez, Enzo Fernández and Nico Paz leading the team. Next Opponents: TBD Alexi's Take: "Most people have Argentina in the top 2, including FIFA, but I'm putting them here. Going to back-to-back World Cup finals and winning in 2022 is impressive, but this is an Argentina team that is now playing without their most important player. Let's be honest, they rode Messi, and he carried them in many ways. They did it willingly and were a wonderful team to watch and obviously incredibly successful. Now we don't know what this team is going to look like going forward without Messi. We have seen Argentina play without Messi, and they have plenty of talent and will continue to be a top-10 team. But it's a changing of a specific guard here – it's not even a change because there's nobody who could ever replace him." 4. Portugal FIFA rank: 7 2026 World Cup Recap: Aside from a 5-0 win over debut team Uzbekistan in the group stage, Cristiano Ronaldo and Co. never lived up to their creative potential. Portugal reached the Round of 16 where they lost to eventual champions Spain. What's Happened Since: If Messi's exit from the world stage was a storybook ending, then Cristiano Ronaldo provided one that felt more like a tabloid. Ronaldo, who had already announced that 2026 would be his last World Cup appearance, had a falling out with manager Jorge Jesus and abruptly left the team in September over disagreements about playing. Portugal still won its four Nations League games – including two victories over Erling Haaland's Norway – and looked crisper without Ronaldo up top. Next Opponents: vs. Czechia (Nov. 14); vs. England (Nov. 17) Alexi's Take: "Having Portugal here is a bit of the opposite reasoning for having Argentina where they are at. I guess we could call it the new Portugal, more than likely now without Cristiano Ronaldo. We have seen how good they are, even recently in this window. I feel like a burden, whether they have admitted it or not, is going to be lifted, and they are just going to get better. Nobody's denying all the talent they have, but this incredible weight (or albatross as some people may say) is now gone. I am bullish on them going forward without Cristiano Ronaldo, just maybe not so bullish when it comes to Argentina without Messi." 3. England 2026 World Cup Recap: With "Wonderwall" providing the soundtrack, there was belief that it would finally come home. England had its best finish at the men's World Cup since 1990 as it reached the semifinals, losing to ancient rivals Argentina and then to France in the bronze match. Harry Kane scored six times this summer, but Jude Bellingham really came into his own at this tournament, with the round-of-16 win over Mexico at the Estadio Azteca etching his name into Three Lions lore. What's Happened Since: Under manager Thomas Tuchel, there will be expectations as always for a major trophy – whether it's in the Nations League or potentially at the Euros in 2028 as hosts. A loss to Spain in September in a Nations League match shouldn't sour those hopes. Next Opponents: vs. Croatia (Nov. 12); vs. Spain (Nov. 15) Alexi's Take: "It hurts me to say England, but they are just a good team. But they are not at the level of the top two teams. But England is always there, and they are as good – and maybe better – than many other teams, even ones in the past that won the World Cup." 2. France FIFA rank: 3 2026 World Cup Recap: The amount of star power in this squad – including forward trio Kylian Mbappé, Ousmane Dembélé, and Michael Olise – had Les Bleus fans thinking this was the team to beat at the tournament. Mbappé scored an astonishing 10 goals at the tournament (making him winner of the Golden Boot for top scorer) and setting a record for most ever in World Cup history with 22. France ran into a brick wall against Spain in the semis but finished in third after a high-scoring consolation match against England. What's Happened Since: With Didier Deschamps stepping down as manager following the World Cup, it felt like an end of an era. But with legend Zinedine Zidane taking over, don't expect France to lose a step – especially with Mbappé, Dembélé, and Olise still in the mix. France won all four of its matches in this window despite Mbappé leaving the team early due to an injury. Next Opponents: vs. Italy (Nov. 12); vs. Türkiye (Nov. 15) Alexi's Take: "This team is just loaded. But the top team did make them look average in the World Cup semifinals." 1. Spain FIFA rank: 12026 World Cup Recap: An improbable run where they only gave up one goal in eight games to win the country's second men's World Cup title ever. Lamine Yamal came into the tournament injured, but La Roja hardly needed the teenage superstar. On their way to the World Cup title, midfield maestro Rodri won the Golden Ball for the tournament's best player and Unai Simón won for the tournament's best keeper. What's Happened Since: Spain's unbeaten streak has now reached 40 games after winning four more times in Nations League action during this past window, including a 3-2 thrilling victory over England at Wembley. Next Opponents: vs. Czechia (Nov. 12); vs. England (Nov. 15)

articles.title: Dodgers-Brewers NLCS Game 1 Will Be Skubal vs. Misiorowski; Yamamoto For Game 2
articles.summary: The starting pitchers are set for Game 1 of the NLCS between the Dodgers and Brewers.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal against the Milwaukee Brewers – who will go with staff ace Jacob Misiorowski – on Sunday in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, last year's World Series MVP, will start Game 2 on Monday at American Family Field, manager Dave Roberts said Friday. Skubal also started Game 1 of the NL Division Series. The two-time Cy Young Award winner pitched six dominant innings, allowing one run and two hits, in a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves. The left-hander struck out seven and walked two. Misiorowski had two starts during the regular season against the Dodgers and a relief appearance in last year's NLCS. In those 17 innings, he has posted a 1.59 ERA with 27 strikeouts and three walks. Yamamoto started Game 3 of the NLDS, and struck out 10 over seven innings. The right-hander allowed one run and four hits to go with one walk. Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell struggled as the Game 2 starter against the Braves, who won 3-2 to tie the best-of-five series 1-1. The Dodgers went on to eliminate the Braves, 3-1. Roberts said the Dodgers were in discussions about adding a pitcher for the best-of-seven NLCS, which would require them to drop a position player. Rosters are due Sunday morning. Miguel Rojas exited Game 3 against the Braves during an at-bat with lower back pain. The utility player underwent imaging, which mostly showed prior back issues. He took ground balls and a couple rounds of batting practice at Dodger Stadium on Friday. Rojas, 37, has said he's leaning toward retiring at the end of the season. "Today was encouraging," Roberts said. "We still have a flight to get on and see how he comes in tomorrow for the workout there, so there’s nothing definitive." The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: FSU football let one big play become a full-blown disaster vs Louisville
articles.summary: Isaac Brown and Louisville's run game thrashed Florida State football's defense, leaving Mike Norvell befuddled.
articles.body:
Stood in the shadow of his own endzone and down 14-0 in the second quarter, Louisville's Isaac Brown took a handoff, jolted left, and zipped past Florida State's defense down the sideline at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium for a 97-yard touchdown run.

The play altered the course of the game and sparked a remarkable Louisville turnaround, which resulted in a 44-20 blowout of the Seminoles on Friday, Oct. 9. The loss extended the program's winless streak away from Doak Campbell Stadium to at least 1,057 days.

After Brown's lengthy touchdown run, Louisville recorded 382 rushing yards and rattled off 35 unanswered points and outscored FSU, 44-6. The Cardinals star back recorded 235 rushing yards and had 313 all-purpose yards after he took the opening kickoff of the second half back 71 yards.

"Isaac was a great player tonight. He's a great player; he really took over the game with the kickoff return and then the big runs that he had," a visibly frustrated FSU head coach Mike Norvell told reporters post-game. "But we can't help great players by not doing and being where we need to be."

Louisville reached the 401 rushing yard mark and finished the game with 397 yards after quarterback Lincoln Kienholz knelt three times in victory formation. It saved the Seminoles (3-3, 1-2 ACC) from officially tying for the most rushing yards allowed in a single game, which remains the 401 allowed against Georgia Tech in 2009, but it in no way lessened the embarrassment.

Of the 397 yards, the most allowed under Norvell and second most in program history, 209 came on three scoring plays: Brown's runs of 97 (a Louisville record) and 68 yards, and a 44-yard score from Braxton Jennings. While the Seminoles' defense has been inconsistent this season, its run defense had been a strength in prior games and had mostly limited explosive plays.

Mike Norvell sounds off after FSU's poor defensive game

Entering the game, FSU allowed an average of 119.2 rushing yards per game, ranked 44th in the country, and was fresh off a dominant display against Virginia, where the defense allowed 37 yards . Despite that, the Cardinals tormented the unit, and it left Norvell befuddled.

"It sucked...," Norvell remarked about his defense while thumping a press conference table. "We gave like 20 freaking yards of rushing a week ago, and this week it was 400 yards.

"It's not because, 'Oh hey, we just forgot to coach this week.' You got to go and be able to execute in the moment. You got to be able to take what you do during the course of the week, yeah, short week and all the things, but that's what we coach and work to play for."

Norvell's blunt characterization of the performance is accurate, and the primary culprit of his frustration was Brown.

With fellow Louisville backfield star Keyjuan Brown out with an injury, Issac Brown had 17 carries and averaged 13.8 per attempt. His two rushing scores of 68+ yards make him one of five active players in FBS to have done that in a single game, according to Opta Stats.

And he breathed life into a Louisville team that looked outmatched in the first quarter.

FSU quickly jumped out to a 14-0 lead, with Ashton Daniels setting a program record for most rushing touchdowns by a quarterback with his 10th of the season. Micahi Danzy added a spectacular one-handed grab for the second score, but fate changed on a fourth-and-goal early in the second quarter.

Daniels screen pass to wide receiver Jasen Lopez was blown up and resulted in a turnover on downs. On the next play from scrimmage, Kienholz handed the ball off to Brown, who blazed past the defense for the 97-yard score.

The touchdown led to Louisville's rout of FSU. It also meant the Seminoles surrendered a double-digit lead and ultimately lost by double digits for the second time this season. The other? The 50-36 loss to Alabama.

"What we saw tonight was not good enough," Norvell said. "It was not good enough coaching, not good enough playing. Not good enough."

Norvell and the Seminoles next head to Miami for a rivalry showdown on Saturday, Oct. 17, before a bye week.

articles.title: Verstappen wins chaotic Singapore GP F1 sprint after Russell crashes
articles.summary: Max Verstappen’s sprint race win was Dutchman’s first of any kind in Singapore as he finished ahead of Lewis Hamilton.
articles.body:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a wet and wild Singapore Grand Prix sprint race on Saturday after George Russell crashed his Mercedes while leading at the end of the opening lap.

Four-time Formula One champion Verstappen held off Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton to win by 2.50 seconds, with Charles Leclerc third as the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri touched and spun on the final lap while in fourth and fifth.

A heavy shower 10 minutes before the scheduled start meant a delay of 30 minutes.

All cars began on intermediate tyres, with some sectors of the Marina Bay Street Circuit much drier than others as the field embarked on two formation laps behind the safety car.

The eventual standing start saw Russell start on the front row alongside pole-sitter Verstappen and it was the Englishman who got away better.

His lead was short-lived as he lost control after touching a treacherous white line on the final bend of the opening lap. He slid sideways into the pit lane wall, bringing out a safety car.

It was another setback in a season of bad luck for Russell, who will start from the back of the grid in Sunday’s Grand Prix because of engine penalties.

“It was a miscalculation,” Russell told Sky Sports. “Came through the corner, had more battery deployment than I thought, pushed me a little bit wider than I hoped and went on to the white line.

It left Hamilton, who had a brilliant start from sixth on the grid, in second place, having leapfrogged Ferrari teammate Leclerc and the two McLarens.

The big beneficiary of Norris and Piastri’s “papaya spat” on the last lap was championship leader Kimi Antonelli , who inherited fourth place in his Mercedes having started seventh on the grid.

Fifth was RB’s Liam Lawson, sixth was the Haas of Oliver Bearman, seventh was Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg and Norris got going again to limp home in eighth and round out the points scorers.

articles.title: 5 Potential Coach Replacements for the Flyers' Rick Tocchet
articles.summary: The 2026-2027 season could've started a whole lot better for the Philadelphia Flyers, but after starting 0-3-2 with just six goals scored and 19 against, the time to worry is now, and that's put head coach Rick Tocchet firmly on the hot seat.
articles.body:
The 2026-2027 season could've started a whole lot better for the Philadelphia Flyers, but after starting 0-3-2 with just six goals scored and 19 against, the time to worry is now, and that's put head coach Rick Tocchet firmly on the hot seat.

After signing a five-year contract, Tocchet helped guide the Flyers to the playoffs last season, and while Philly advanced to the second round before being ushered out quickly by eventual Stanley Cup champion Carolina, that success raised expectations for this season. The Flyers' grim start, therefore, could come with consequences and leave general manager Danny Brière with the options of moving on from Tocchet, making rash trades, or both.

Trades take two sides to make a deal, and firing a coach needs only the GM to make the call. If the Flyers move on from Tocchet, who's out there to take over? We'll take a look at potential candidates for the Flyers and their young and impressionable roster.

If there's someone who would make a lot of sense to coach a young Flyers team and has experience in Philadelphia, former Edmonton Oilers coach Kris Knoblauch would be it.

Knoblauch coached the Oilers for the past two and a half seasons and helped lead them to two straight Stanley Cup Finals and three total playoff appearances. The Oilers bowing out in the first round to Anaheim last year ended up being his undoing, although Edmonton management having their eyes on Mike Babcock may have had more to do with that decision than anything.

Knoblauch's first NHL coaching job, however, came as an assistant coach with the Flyers from 2017 to 2019 under Dave Hakstol before he moved on to be a head coach in the AHL with Hartford. With a successful tenure in Edmonton and a history of experience coaching successful young players in the OHL with Erie (where he coached Connor McDavid, Alex DeBrincat, Dylan Strome, and others), he would be a front-runner for any opening in the NHL, but especially in Philadelphia.

If the Flyers wanted to make a splash, if they moved on from Rick Tocchet, bringing in a Stanley Cup-winning coach like Bruce Cassidy would do it.

Cassidy led the Vegas Golden Knights to the Stanley Cup in 2023 and also coached the Boston Bruins to the Final in 2019. Since reviving his career as a head coach with the Bruins, he's done nothing but win where he's gone, albeit with a bit of a shelf life before the mood changes.

Cassidy's firing from Vegas last season led to John Tortorella taking over and then guiding the Golden Knights to the Stanley Cup Final, where they lost to Carolina. The team's makeup wasn't any different, but Torts' no-nonsense approach was handled better by the players than Cassidy's tough, direct style.

Cassidy would get results in Philly, no doubt, but the question would be whether or not his style would mesh with what Brière and Keith Jones are trying to establish with the Flyers. Boston and Vegas were veteran teams built to win, but the Flyers are looking to build on the sudden progress from last year. It would be a fascinating setup should "Butch" go to Philadelphia.

The one caveat? Cassidy's availability. He was a strong candidate for the Oilers job this summer, only for Vegas to block his move because he was still under contract with the Golden Knights. It'd be interesting to see if Vegas would allow him to coach across the country.

Unlike some of the other possible new Flyers coaches, Jay Woodcroft as a possibility comes with some potentially dramatic wrinkles.

Woodcroft is a guy who has been in the running for numerous head coaching jobs over the past few years since he was fired by the Edmonton Oilers in November 2023, but last season he landed on Joel Quenneville's bench as an assistant with the Anaheim Ducks.

The relationship between the Flyers and Ducks would best be described as "frosty" after everything that's gone on with Cutter Gauthier forcing his way out of Philly to go to Anaheim and then the Flyers signing Leo Carlsson to a monster offer sheet this summer. You'd like to believe that if the Flyers wanted to hire Woodcroft as their new head coach, Ducks GM Pat Verbeek wouldn't stand in his way, but that would be a fascinating phone call to make regardless.

Woodcroft has a ton of NHL coaching experience outside of his brief tenure behind the Oilers' bench, and he's going to be a head coach again one of these years, and the Flyers would make for a great opportunity for him to show what he can do.

The easiest and quickest move to make if the Flyers fire Rick Tocchet would be to look right next to him on the bench, assistant coach Todd Reirden.

Reirden has a long history of assistant work with the Flyers, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Washington Capitals. He also has some head coaching experience from his time in Washington, where he led the Capitals to the playoffs in 2019 but was fired midseason the following year.

While Reirden would be the easiest move to make, he wouldn't make the sexiest pick, and if he took over as anything more than an interim, we're sure the panic levels amongst the Flyers fan base would reach new heights. If the Flyers move on from Tocchet, they'll assuredly be aiming bigger.

If you're not familiar with John Snowden, that's understandable because he's relatively new in the coaching ranks.

Snowden was hired as head coach of the Flyers' AHL team in Lehigh Valley last season after he was an assistant coach there the previous two years. Before that, he was with the Toronto Marlies as an assistant and spent six seasons as an assistant and head coach in the ECHL with Orlando and Newfoundland, and one season as the director of hockey operations there as well. He's 44 years old and climbing the ladder.

Despite all of Snowden's prior experience, he finally became an AHL head coach a year ago, and although AHL head coaches are often heirs to the NHL throne when things go wrong, it would be a gutsy choice by Danny Brière to promote Snowden to the Flyers so quickly, but if fans are tired of seeing the same coaches cycle through new jobs, promoting Snowden would certainly run counter to that.

articles.title: De la rivalidad en el Tour al abrazo en Cartagena: Chris Froome llena de elogios a Nairo Quintana y a Colombia
articles.standfirst: Chris Froome habló de su gran rivalidad con Nairo Quintana y le envió un mensaje a Colombia
articles.summary: Chris Froome habló de su gran rivalidad con Nairo Quintana y le envió un mensaje a Colombia
articles.body: Durante más de una década, los nombres de Chris Froome y Nairo Quintana fueron sinónimo de los ataques más feroces en la alta montaña del ciclismo internacional. Sin embargo, el tiempo transforma las batallas deportivas en respeto mutuo, y así quedó demostrado con el arribo del tetracampeón del Tour de Francia a Cartagena para participar en la edición del Gran Fondo Nairo Fest. A su llegada al Aeropuerto Internacional Rafael Núñez, el pedalista británico fue recibido con un cálido y emotivo abrazo por parte del propio Nairo Quintana. El encuentro dio paso a declaraciones cargadas de nostalgia, admiración y gratitud por parte del histórico corredor del Team Sky (hoy Israel-Premier Tech). Al ser consultado sobre los años de intensa competencia que mantuvo contra el boyacense en Europa, Froome no escatimó en reconocimientos hacia la figura de Quintana: "Estoy muy orgulloso de estar aquí, muy feliz de poder compartir este momento especial con Nairo y con tantos fanáticos en Colombia. Tuvimos batallas increíbles en las montañas europeas durante muchos años y siempre fue un rival excepcional." Los enfrentamientos entre ambos definieron una era dorada del ciclismo moderno, especialmente en las ediciones del Tour de Francia de 2013 y 2015, donde Quintana terminó como subcampeón por detrás del británico, así como en la Vuelta a España 2016, que quedó en manos del colombiano tras un duelo memorable. Además de recordar sus etapas de gloria, Froome dedicó unas palabras al público colombiano y a la afición que siempre lo ha recibido con entusiasmo en cada una de sus visitas al país. Destacó la pasión única con la que los colombianos viven el deporte de las bielas y la huella que referentes como Nairo, Egan Bernal y Rigoberto Urán han dejado en el pelotón mundial. El evento en Cartagena sirve como un marco especial en la agenda del ciclismo nacional, marcando el reencuentro de dos leyendas vivas que pasaron de disputarse el maillot amarillo a pedalear juntos en ambiente de celebración.

articles.title: La Dimayor sanciona a Independiente Medellín tras la agresión con moneda a Daniel Torres
articles.standfirst: Sanción del Medellín por el monedazo a Daniel Torres: Dimayor confirmó el castigo
articles.summary: Sanción del Medellín por el monedazo a Daniel Torres: Dimayor confirmó el castigo
articles.body: El Comité Disciplinario de la Dimayor hizo oficial la sanción en contra de Independiente Medellín tras los violentos hechos ocurridos durante el partido frente a Independiente Santa Fe, en los que el mediocampista cardenal —y exjugador del equipo antioqueño— Daniel Torres resultó herido en el rostro por un objeto lanzado desde la tribuna. Mediante la Resolución No. 101 del 9 de octubre de 2026, el ente rector del fútbol colombiano determinó impartir un castigo doble a la institución antioqueña: El incidente tuvo lugar el pasado lunes 5 de octubre cuando Daniel Torres fue sustituido en el minuto 76. Mientras abandonaba el terreno de juego y saludaba a los espectadores, una moneda impactó directamente su rostro, provocándole un corte sangrante en la entreceja. El partido debió detenerse durante tres minutos para que el cuerpo médico atendiera al jugador. Posteriormente, el propio Daniel Torres interpuso la denuncia ante la Fiscalía General de la Nación para iniciar el proceso judicial contra los responsables. A pesar de que la defensa del Independiente Medellín argumentó que se trató de un acto individual que no representaba a toda la hinchada, la norma del Código Disciplinario de la FCF responsabiliza a los clubes por la conducta de sus espectadores. No obstante, tanto la Dimayor como las autoridades destacaron que el trabajo conjunto con el club permitió identificar a los presuntos responsables del ataque mediante el material de video de las cámaras de seguridad del escenario deportivo, lo que facilitará el avance de los procesos judiciales e individuales.

articles.title: Arsenal beat Leeds 2-1 in comeback win to move level with Man City at top
articles.summary: Arsenal come from behind to beat Leeds United moving them joint top of the Premier League with Manchester City.
articles.body:
Arsenal roared back to beat Leeds 2-1 and pull level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League on Saturday, hitting the ground running after the three-week international break.

Mikel Arteta’s champions struggled to impose themselves against well-organised opponents in the first half but found their mojo after half-time to make it five wins from six games this season.

Defender James Justin gave Leeds a deserved lead early in the second half at the Emirates, silencing the home crowd in the October sunshine.

But Arsenal were level minutes later through Riccardo Calafiori and substitute Bruno Guimaraes scored what turned out to be the winner after a finely crafted team goal.

The focus returned to the pitch on Saturday after the bombshell announcement that City had been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

But Arsenal, who had a perfect record before their 3-0 defeat by Brighton last month, struggled to break down Daniel Farke’s physical team in the first half.

Noni Madueke, overlooked by Thomas Tuchel for England’s most recent squad, was handed a rare start on the left of the Gunners’ attack in place of the injured Christos Tzolis.

But neither he nor Bukayo Saka on the other flank had much joy against a defence that had conceded just three league goals all season.

Leeds had a couple of half-chances late in the first half.

First, Jayden Bogle and Anton Stach got in each other’s way as Stach struck the ball against his teammate. Then Bogle was denied from close range by Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya, who was out quickly to smother his shot.

Raya also got down smartly to keep out a shot from Leeds defender Gabriel Gudmundsson from a tight angle.

Arsenal managed just one shot on target in the whole of the first half, but the game opened up after the break, with chances at both ends.

Impressive Leeds midfielder Ao Tanaka forced Raya to tip over before Justin put his side ahead in the 55th minute, finishing sweetly from just inside the box after a Gudmundsson cross following a well-worked move down the left.

Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes got a touch with his head but failed to keep the ball out of the net.

But the Gunners were back level just seven minutes later when the unmarked Calafiori finished past England international goalkeeper James Trafford after being set up by Ben White.

Worse was to come for Leeds when Guimaraes finished powerfully after some neat play down the Arsenal left, with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all involved.

The win takes Arsenal to 15 points, behind leaders City on goal difference.

Enzo Maresca’s City, with a game in hand, are braced for a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday following the announcement of their guilty verdict last week.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Man City: Premier League – teams, prediction, Haaland, charges
articles.summary: Man City travel to Liverpool for their first game since being found guilty of serious EPL financial breaches.
articles.body:
Who : Liverpool vs Manchester City What : Premier League, matchday 6 Where : Anfield, Liverpool, United Kingdom When : Sunday, October 11, at 4:30pm local time (15:30 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 12:30 GMT.

Manchester City will face the full fury of Anfield on Sunday when the Premier League leaders confront old rivals Liverpool in their first game since being found guilty of breaking the competition’s financial rules .

City can expect a hostile reception from Liverpool fans after an independent commission found they arranged “sham” deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2bn) between 2009 and 2018.

The financial breaches occurred during a period in which City won three Premier League titles and numerous other trophies, with Liverpool struggling to break the Etihad Stadium outfit’s silverware monopoly.

City have appealed against the devastating verdict and manager Enzo Maresca was bullish that they will overturn the original ruling. But the Premier League season is now stuck in stasis awaiting a ruling on the appeal and any potential sanction.

Liverpool supporters have often created a febrile atmosphere for City’s visits since they emerged as title contenders following the takeover by their Abu Dhabi-based owners in 2008.

This weekend’s showdown is likely to set a new standard for vitriol directed at City’s players and fans.

What is the controversy surrounding Man City?

An independent commission found Man City guilty of nearly all of the 115 charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

The Premier League said the commission found that City used schemes during the affected period to appear to comply with financial rules.

City have continued to protest their innocence and have lodged an appeal , but if the decision is upheld, then points deductions, fines, transfer embargoes and relegation are all possible punishments for the club.

‘A brutal day’ awaits Man City at Anfield

A social media post promoting a “Bus greeting” has urged Liverpool supporters to gather near ‌‌the stadium several hours before kickoff with flags, banners, pyrotechnics and flares ahead of the arrival of the City players’ bus.

Merseyside Police said there would be an appropriate policing operation ⁠⁠in place on the day.

“If they want an understanding of how angry the game is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe,” former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville said on The Overlap podcast.

“I suspect there may be banners, there will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield … it will be a brutal day.”

Over the past 12 years, Liverpool have finished second to City on three occasions. Only one of those, in 2013-14, came during the period under scrutiny in this financial breach controversy.

But City’s rivals believe the wrongdoing in that period built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who stepped down at the end of last season.

Opta’s supercomputer has handed City a 40.7 percent chance of victory on Sunday.

Liverpool have a 34.6 percent probability, while there is a 24.7 percent chance of a draw.

In his pre-match conference on Friday, Man City’s manager Maresca said he has absolute faith the club will win its appeal and rejected any suggestion that City’s haul of silverware over the past 15 years was now tainted.

“I completely trust the club,” said Maresca, who was appointed manager in June but also previously worked at City as part of Guardiola’s coaching staff.

“I trust the club because I trust the people and this is also the reason why I joined the club. … There is not another club in the world where I would like to be.”

His Liverpool counterpart, Andoni Iraola, said the lack of clarity over City’s future is causing uncertainty throughout the Premier League.

“I think the worst thing probably is the uncertainty, that no one knows what’s going to happen,” Iraola said.

“But we have to focus on Liverpool – be the best club we can be, the best team we can be and that’s my challenge.”

How have Man City and Liverpool played this season?

While off the field, Man City are embroiled in a huge controversy; on the pitch, they’ve been the best team this season.

City are top of the Premier League’s points table with 15 points, winning all five games so far.

Liverpool are sixth in the standings, having won twice and drawn three times. They are on nine points, six behind City.

When did Man City and Liverpool last meet?

Man City and Liverpool last met on April 4 this year in the FA Cup quarterfinals.

Erling Haaland scored a hat-trick and Antoine Semenyo added another goal as City thrashed Liverpool 4-0 at the Etihad.

Liverpool vs Man City: Last five Premier League matches

Liverpool 1-2 Man City (February 8, 2026)

Man City 3-0 Liverpool (November 9, 2025)

Man City 0-2 Liverpool (February 23, 2025)

Liverpool 2-0 Man City (December 1, 2024)

(Last five matches, latest first; only Premier League games)

Liverpool were handed a huge blow ahead of Sunday’s heavyweight clash, with attackers Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo both ruled out.

Both players returned from international duty with injuries. Gakpo picked up an ankle injury playing for the Netherlands against Serbia, while Isak suffered what ⁠⁠Iraola described as a “small” thigh injury with Sweden against Romania.

Isak’s absence is a significant blow after the striker had finally found his form, scoring four goals in the opening five league games.

Neither injury is believed to be long-term, with Gakpo’s availability depending on how he copes with the pain while the club monitors both players day by day.

Man City’s Haaland fit to face Liverpool

Haaland’s involvement against Liverpool had been in doubt after the striker came off during Norway’s Nations League loss to Portugal earlier this month.

But that was understood to be a precautionary measure amid an intense run of games during an extended international break.

Maresca has confirmed that Haaland, who has scored 169 goals in 205 games for the club, is available for their trip to Merseyside.

“He’s good. He went to Marbella, [had] two, three days off, played golf, recovery,” the City boss revealed. “Ready for Anfield. He’s good.”

Predicted lineups: Liverpool vs Manchester City

Probable Liverpool XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Jeremie Frimpong, Ronald Araujo, Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez; Ryan Gravenberch, Alexis Mac Allister; Victor Munoz, Szoboszlai, Bradley Barcola; Florian Wirtz

Probable Man City XI (4-2-3-1): Gianluigi Donnarumma; Matheus Nunes, Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi, Josko Gvardiol; Enzo Fernandez, Eliott Anderson; Jeremy Doku, Rayan Cherki, Iliman Ndiaye; Erling Haaland

articles.title: Portugal suspends Cristiano Ronaldo and initiates disciplinary proceedings after walkout
articles.summary: The Portuguese Football Federation has suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for walking out on the team and initiated disciplinary proceedings.
articles.body: The Portuguese Football Federation has suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for walking out on the team and initiated disciplinary proceedings. The case has been referred to its disciplinary investigation committee and its findings will remain confidential until its conclusions are reached, the federation said in a statement Saturday. The 41-year-old Ronaldo left the Portugal camp during the international window in a dispute with new coach Jorge Jesus over his lack of playing time in the Nations League. In the three games Ronaldo was either an unused substitute or absent, Portugal won, and his replacement Gonçalo Ramos seized his chance by scoring three goals. Ronaldo was involved only in Portugal’s opening Nations League game, where he was replaced by Ramos in a 1-0 win over Wales. He left the squad after watching the second game from the substitutes’ bench — a 2-1 win in Norway — and Portugal showed no ill effects from his departure with wins over Denmark and Norway to book a quarterfinal. Ronaldo ended the international break with a long post to his 679 million followers on Instagram, where he asked the Portugal coach to acknowledge a mistake in asking him to warm up on the sidelines in Oslo and then not send him on the field. Jesus did not acknowledge any mistake. The star wrote that he expected a suspension under federation rules but promised his fans “we will have one or more farewell matches.” Ronaldo could possibly face a harsh punishment for leaving the training camp. The federation’s disciplinary regulations say that any player who “abandons or fails to appear” without justification at a training session, match or activity of the national teams “shall be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months,” in addition to a fine. Ronaldo did tell the federation he was leaving, but it wasn’t clear whether the decision would be considered justified in accordance with the regulations. “I have already apologized, but I know that actions must have consequences,” Ronaldo wrote in his statement. “Anyone in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.”

articles.title: Rangers goalie Igor Shesterkin out for the season after suffering lower-body injury
articles.summary: Shesterkin was injured in the second period of Friday night's loss to the Capitals.
articles.body:
New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin is out for the season after suffering a lower-body injury during Friday's loss to the Washington Capitals, the team announced.

Shesterkin was injured during the second period and had to be helped off the ice, unable to put any weight on his right leg. The Rangers did not reveal exactly what happened to the 30-year-old netminder.

During a scramble in the Rangers' defensive end, Shesterkin jammed his right skate into the goal post while trying to reposition himself for a save. The leg then appeared to awkwardly bend as he collapsed in the crease.

"It's awful," said Rangers captain J.T. Miller afterward. "He's a pillar of this team. It stinks. … We don't even know what's going on, but to see him leave the game is a shot to all of us, a shock to all of us. But at the same time, it means we got to step up to a man to try to get the job done, especially [backup Dylan Garand]."

Garand, the team's fourth-round draft pick in 2020, is now the Rangers' No. 1 goalie. He has five career NHL starts and stopped 11 of 12 shots against the Capitals after coming in for Shesterkin.

Shesterkin is in his eighth NHL season, all with the Rangers. He won the Vezina Trophy in 2021-22 as the league's top goaltender and was also named a First-Team All-Star that season. This is the second season of an eight-year, $92.475 million extension he signed in Aug. 2021.

Through five starts, Shesterkin was 3-1-0 with a .935 even strength save percentage and was a little over a week removed from scoring the first goalie goal in Rangers history.

That wasn't the only bad goalie news the Rangers announced on Saturday. Backup Joonas Korpisalo, who was already considered week-to-week with a lower-body injury, will miss an additional four weeks as he recovers.

articles.title: WAP! DOPAMINE FEST convierte Madrid en un punto de encuentro entre fitness, bienestar y ocio
articles.standfirst: El Nuevo Ático de la Estación de Chamartín acoge este sábado un festival que reúne deporte, música, gastronomía y comunidad bajo el concepto de "social wellness"
articles.summary: El Nuevo Ático de la Estación de Chamartín acoge este sábado un festival que reúne deporte, música, gastronomía y comunidad bajo el concepto de "social wellness"
articles.body: Madrid acoge este sábado, 10 de octubre, la primera edición de WAP! DOPAMINE FEST, un macroencuentro urbano que une fitness, wellness, música, gastronomía y comunidad en una misma experiencia. El festival, que se celebra en el Nuevo Ático de la Estación de Chamartín, propone una forma diferente de entender el bienestar, alejándose de la idea de que el ejercicio físico está ligado exclusivamente al entrenamiento y al rendimiento. La iniciativa responde al auge de nuevas comunidades vinculadas al running, el cycling, el yoga o el entrenamiento funcional, que han convertido la actividad física en una forma de socialización y ocio. Bajo esta premisa, WAP! DOPAMINE FEST apuesta por el concepto de "social wellness", un modelo en el que el bienestar no se vive únicamente de manera individual, sino también a través de las experiencias compartidas y el sentimiento de pertenencia a una comunidad. La propuesta se articula alrededor de cinco pilares: fitness, wellness, música, gastronomía y comunidad. A lo largo de la jornada, los asistentes pueden participar en actividades como running, cycling, boxing, pilates, yoga, barre o recovery, además de disfrutar de sesiones con DJs y diferentes propuestas gastronómicas relacionadas con la nutrición y la hidratación. Uno de los elementos diferenciales del festival es su estructura. En lugar de seguir una programación cerrada alrededor de un escenario principal, los asistentes pueden recorrer los diferentes espacios y construir su propia experiencia, alternando actividades de alta intensidad con otras centradas en la recuperación y el descanso. El recinto cuenta con distintas zonas temáticas dedicadas a disciplinas y actividades como HYROX, ciclo, zumba, ritmos latinos y urbanos, boxeo, pilates, yoga, barre, flamenco fit, running y recovery. El festival también dispone de una zona infantil, denominada Kids Zone. Los espacios, tanto interiores como exteriores, permiten combinar entrenamientos, sesiones de recuperación, baños de hielo y propuestas de nutrición y gastronomía con música y momentos de socialización. La idea es que cada persona pueda adaptar la jornada a sus intereses, independientemente de su nivel de actividad física o de su experiencia deportiva. El nombre WAP!, acrónimo de We Are Power!, resume la filosofía del proyecto: entender la energía no solo como rendimiento físico, sino también como algo que se genera al compartir experiencias. Por ello, instructores, marcas, clubes de running, estudios de yoga, comunidades fitness, influencers y asistentes forman parte de un mismo entorno. WAP! DOPAMINE FEST busca así acercar el fitness y el wellness a los códigos de los festivales contemporáneos, con la música, la gastronomía, el descubrimiento y la interacción social como protagonistas. Una propuesta que reivindica el cuidado personal como una forma de ocio y una experiencia colectiva. El festival se celebra este sábado de 09:00 a 20:30 horas en el Nuevo Ático de la Estación de Chamartín, situado en la calle Agustín de Foxá, 40, en Madrid.

articles.summary: Nicolai Remberg is facing a potential lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a suspected cruciate ligament injury during Hamburger SV's 3-2 comeback...
articles.body:
Nicolai Remberg is facing a potential lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a suspected cruciate ligament injury during Hamburger SV's 3-2 comeback victory over TSG Hoffenheim on Saturday.

The HSV captain was forced off late in the first half following a challenge from Hoffenheim's Bambasé Conté, with head coach Merlin Polzin offering a worrying assessment of the injury after the match.

"It looks absolutely awful. There is definitely a suspicion of a cruciate ligament injury," Polzin told reporters.

"It is a bitter moment, not just for him personally but also for us as a team. We are hoping for the best, but it doesn't look good."

Losing their captain for an extended period would represent a significant blow for HSV, who climbed to 11th in the Bundesliga table with Saturday's victory.

articles.title: Chelsea Gray’s ‘legendary’ A’ja Wilson comments despite Valkyries sweep of Aces
articles.summary: As the Las Vegas Aces lost in Game 3 to the Golden State Valkyries, 87-77, the reigning champions have been eliminated from the playoffs as superstar A’ja W...
articles.body:
As the Las Vegas Aces lost in Game 3 to the Golden State Valkyries, 87-77, the reigning champions have been eliminated from the playoffs as superstar A'ja Wilson and the rest of the team will regroup in the offseason for next season. It was another superb season for Wilson after the Aces star won her fifth MVP award, as teammate Chelsea Gray had an emotional response when talking about the 30-year-old.

Speaking after the disappointing loss, the 34-year-old guard would be asked about Wilson this season, expressing how she has been "legendary" this season. Winning her fifth MVP, Wilson averaged 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.9 blocks, and 1.4 steals per game while shooting 52.7 percent from the field and 40.4 percent from three-point range this season.

"I get to play with the best every single day, and it's the player, and it's the person," Gray said after she recorded 17 points, five rebounds, and five assists in Friday's loss. "We have our own dynamic relationship that's…It's like playful, it's honest, it's raw, it's having each other's back, and I'm super proud of what she's been able to do."

Chelsea Gray continues on Aces' A'ja Wilson

In the Game 3 loss to Golden State, Wilson would score 21 points on six of 19 shooting from the field, one of four from deep, and made eight of 11 from the free-throw line to go along with 10 rebounds, two blocks, a steal, and an assist. Subsequently, Gray would candidly go into how she feels about Wilson and how the team "demands a lot" from her.

"She's great, she's our leader," Gray said. "She expects a lot of herself on both ends of the floor. And when you're in the conversation to be MVP, to be defensive player of the year every single year, you're getting everybody's best shot. She's doing things that haven't been heard of, and she's doing it her way, unapologetically herself as a strong Black woman. And I just I really appreciate that and being around that constantly."

At any rate, Wilson, Gray, and Las Vegas look to prepare for next season and hope to once again be in title contention.

articles.title: Georgia Redcoat's pep band cancels trip to Alabama game in aftermath of storm
articles.summary: The Georgia Redcoat pep band canceled its trip to the Alabama game due to safety concerns from post-tropical cyclone Isaias. Here are the details.
articles.body:
Georgia football 's game at Alabama Saturday night is expected to kick off as scheduled, but the Redcoat Band's pep band isn't making the trip due to Isaias.

The storm that was downgraded from a hurricane to a post-tropical cyclone caused damage due to high winds, fallen trees and heavy rain. Georgia Power said about 56,000 customers in the state were still without power at 10 .a.m., and another 60,000 customers had power restored.

About 80 members of the Derbies Pep Band were planning to attend the game as the only Redcoat members scheduled for the 7:30 p.m. ET contest, band director Brett Bawcum said in an email to the Athens Banner-Herald Saturday afternoon.

He said they were scheduled to travel on two buses to Tuscaloosa Saturday afternoon and then back to Athens after the game Saturday night.

"Out of an abundance of caution, the Derbies Pep Band will not be in attendance at today's game," the Redcoat Band posted in an Instagram story.

It said the band had extensive communication over several days with Georgia athletics, the University of Georgia administration and emergency personnel and travel partners.

"We appreciate the partnership in prioritizing the safety of our students and staff," the statement said. "We'll still be cheering just as loudly from Athens! Go Dawgs!"

Isaias was about 50 miles south of Birmingham at 10 a.m. Saturday, moving north-northwest at 10 mph, according to the National Hurricane Center, with sustained winds of up to 35 miles per hour with stronger gusts possible.

Wind advisories remain in effect in Birmingham and Tuscaloosa until 7 p.m. CDT. There is an 80% chance of rain in Tuscaloosa during the day and 50% at night.

articles.body:
It's a bit hard to talk about the full fantasy football fallout for the rumored Marvin Harrison Jr. trade , given that we don't know where he's going yet as of publishing this (that hasn't stopped us from speculating where he MIGHT be going ).

But we do know that Harrison Jr. will be inactive this week ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the Detroit Lions (which, ironically, might have been a great spot for Harrison Jr. to flourish, oh well). And if a trade is being finalized, it might mean that by next week, we'll know what this means for the Cardinals .

But let's summarize it here: This is huge news for Michael Wilson, who had already become the WR1 in Arizona before this deal. Yes, tight end Trey McBride is arguably the No. 1 target in the passing game. But Wilson has just one fewer target than McBride and 16 more yards right now. It might be a tiny boost for Kendrick Bourne (who had eight catches for 75 yards in Week 1). But the focus here is on Wilson, who will cement himself as a WR2 the rest of the season with this trade.

articles.title: Mets Trade Idea For Ronald Acuña Jr. Faces Reality Check
articles.summary: A trade for Ronald Acuña Jr. is floated for the Mets, but the cost and division rules make it a near-impossible feat for owner Steve Cohen.
articles.body:
The most surprising fact about the Mets and Ronald Acuña Jr. is that the trade idea itself is likely dead on arrival. While John Perrotto of Yahoo Sports laid out a specific plan to swap players, the financial and structural barriers are too high to clear. The Braves would never move their star within the division, and the Mets simply do not have the young talent needed to match Acuña's value.

Acuña just finished a rough postseason for Atlanta. During the 2026 playoffs, he recorded just three hits and four runs across seven games, batting only .125. This poor showing might make some think the Braves want to move him. But his regular season numbers tell a different story. He hit .255 with 104 hits, 20 home runs, 55 RBIs, and 61 runs in 107 games. A team does not trade a player with that kind of production just because of a few bad weeks.

The trade idea from Perrotto suggests the Mets send left-hander Zac Thornton and 19-year-old prospect Bruin Agbayani to Atlanta. Thornton is 24 and had a fine rookie season with a 3.32 ERA in 15 starts. MLB Pipeline ranks Agbayani as the 28th-best prospect among the Mets. These are good young players, but they are not enough to get Acuña.

Mets owner Steve Cohen has deep pockets, but he cannot buy this specific player. Perrotto wrote, "Mets owner Steve Cohen would love to add Acuña to his star-studded roster." That desire is clear. The problem is the cost. The writer noted, "However, they probably couldn't make an offer strong enough to swing a trade."

Even if Cohen adds more pieces, the Braves have no reason to sell. They are in the same division. Trading a star to a rival that sits right next door is bad business. The Mets already have Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor. Adding Acuña would make the lineup scary, but it would not help the team win more than keeping their current core intact.

There is another star player in the mix for New York, but the path is just as hard. The prospect of acquiring Bryce Harper from the Phillies was discussed on the Oct. 7 "Baseball Tonight in New York" edition. SNY's Jim Duquette discussed the hurdles. "There would be a lot of hoops to have to go through," Duquette said.

Harper has a no-trade clause, which gives him power. Duquette noted that Harper might be willing to move because he does not see eye to eye with Phillies president Dave Dombrowski. But the Phillies need outfielders, and the Mets need a first baseman. The question remains if the Mets would give up A.J. Ewing and other assets for a player in his mid-30s.

Perrotto sees the Mets adding one more intriguing young piece as part of the Acuña trade idea. He wrote, "Moreover, Perrotto sees New York adding one more intriguing young piece as part of this trade idea that could entice the Braves to consider a Mets offer." That piece is Agbayani. He played in just 18 professional games since being drafted by the Twins. He is a high-upside kid, but he is not a finished product.

The reality is that the Mets will likely stick with what they have. The roster is built around Soto and Lindor. Chasing a star like Acuña or Harper requires giving up the future for a short-term boost. The Braves know their value. They will not sell low, and they will not sell to a rival. The trade idea is fun to read, but it will not happen.

articles.title: Joe Cole explains what helped Arsenal get over the line against Leeds
articles.summary: Joe Cole says Arsenal’s remarkable squad depth was helpful as they beat Leeds in a match they could have lost and did not play at their best. Leeds headed to...
articles.body:
Joe Cole says Arsenal's remarkable squad depth was helpful as they beat Leeds in a match they could have lost and did not play at their best. Leeds headed to London as one of the most in-form teams in the league, and a lot of their players had the chance to rest during the international window, so they were fresh.

However, as champions, Arsenal is always expected to perform, and the Gunners knew they had to respond to their loss to Brighton just before the break . They tried their best to make that happen and eventually managed to overturn Leeds' opening goal to secure an important win in the fixture, which made them remind everyone why they are champions.

It was not an easy game, and Mikel Arteta had to be tactically spot-on to get a win, especially after his team went behind and they responded well to get back to win. One luxury Arsenal has over some of their rivals is depth, and Cole says it helped them to find a way to break down a very stubborn Leeds team. He said via the BBC :

"Leeds look like they've ran out of ideas. It's what champions do and Arsenal have got the squad depth. They've got the quality and they all work hard for each other."

The win is a statement of intent, showing Arsenal can grind out results even when not at their best. The character and unity within the squad will please the fans, and the momentum from this victory could be crucial in the weeks ahead. Arteta's side will look to build on this as they chase their ambitions.

Leeds will take heart from their performance, even in defeat, as they showed they can compete with the best. Their unbeaten run may have ended, but the display suggests they are genuine contenders for European places. Farke's side will look to bounce back quickly.

articles.title: J.J. Watt is confused like Texans fans on trade rumors for Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. is getting traded, right? Well maybe. Even J.J. Watt is confused.
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr. is getting traded, right?

Well what's the asking price and which team is making the move?

When J.J. Watt is confused as the public, you know the clickbait conversation is alive and well.

The former Houston Texans three-time Defensive Player of the Year recipient is like many who can't seem to comprehend the news surrounding the third-year Arizona Cardinals wide receiver. While the Texans have been rumored to be in the hunt for Harrison's services, ESPN's Adam Schefter never said which team was willing to pull the trigger.

The only thing fans know right now is that Harrison will be traded, so Watt had to weigh in online.

It would be one thing if Harrison knew where he was being traded, but talks were stalling to work out the final pieces. Therin lies the problem, he stll doesn't know where he'll be playing for the rest of the regular season.

And while Houston, desperate to add another offensive piece to the puzzle in hopes ot making a postseason push, the deal could have been leaked to see if Arizona could get a better price from another team in the mix. Currently, the early expectation is that Houston will trade a 2028 second-round pick.

Arizona, which earlier this week mentioned it wasn't interested in moving off Harrison, has wanted a 2027 second-round pick as the starting point for deals.

While Watt would perhaps love to see Harrison head to Houston, the reporting itself remains nothing more than a clickbait headline with lttle juice for the time being.

The Texans hope to add some juice to the stat sheet with a win this Sunday against the Tennessee Titans in Nasvhille.

articles.title: ‘He’s Got to Be Aggressive’: Broncos’ Bo Nix Finds Himself at Center of Sean Payton’s Latest Move
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton has taken back offensive play-calling duties from Davis Webb after the team’s first four games of the 2026 season....
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton has taken back offensive play-calling duties from Davis Webb after the team's first four games of the 2026 season. The move comes as the Broncos look to improve their offensive performance.

The Broncos are 2-2, with Bo Nix and the offense struggling to produce consistent results . Payton will now call the plays, while Webb remains the team's offensive coordinator.

Sean Payton reclaims Broncos' offensive play-calling duties

Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton will resume play-calling duties beginning with the Broncos Week 5 game. Webb had been given the responsibility before the season began, but Payton has now decided to call the offensive plays himself.

The Broncos are 2-2 after four games. They lost to the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers but defeated the Jacksonville Jaguars and Los Angeles Rams. Under Webb's play-calling, Denver averaged 280.3 total yards and 18.5 points per game across those four contests.

The Broncos also struggled to score consistently in the first half. Denver scored 40 first-half points across its first four games. Against San Francisco, however, both teams managed only three points before halftime. The 49ers later pulled away for a 24-14 victory.

Bo Nix has recorded 819 passing yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions through four games. Nix has contributed less as a runner than he did during the 2025 season. In 2025, Nix finished with 356 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns. Through the first four games of the 2026 season, he has managed just 25 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.

NFL analyst Daniel Jeremiah discussed Denver's offense during the October 10 episode of The Rich Eisen Show. Speaking about Webb's work and what Nix needs to do, Jeremiah said , "I think Davis Webb has done that to a decent degree. It's just getting Bo Nix to kind of get his stinger back and get him to just let it rip and play more aggressive.

"I think they got guys open. You can watch the tape, and you're like, there's guys there. He's not throwing the football. So that's again, that's not the play design. It's not the play call. It's not the timing. It's just he's got to be aggressive."

Webb will remain the Broncos' offensive coordinator despite losing play-calling duties. He will continue to help prepare the game plan and take part in offensive meetings, while Bo Nix has struggled through the team's first four games .

The Denver Broncos will face the Los Angeles Chargers on October 11 at SoFi Stadium. Denver enters the game after a loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The Broncos also lost 31-10 to the Kansas City Chiefs earlier this season but defeated the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-13 and the Los Angeles Rams 30-26.

Head coach Sean Payton assessed the team's performance, saying , "certainly this isn't championship football, what we see. How quickly can we correct those things?"

Denver will be without Patrick Surtain II, who is sidelined with an ankle injury. His absence means the Broncos will be missing an important cornerback as they prepare to defend against the Chargers' passing attack. Riley Moss will also miss the game because of a rib injury, leaving Denver without both starting cornerbacks.

Pat Bryant is also unavailable after being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. Before his injury, he recorded nine receptions for 133 receiving yards and one touchdown this season.

Meanwhile, Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack has recorded three sacks through the first four games. The Broncos offensive line will face a difficult assignment against Mack.

The Week 5 game will be the first test of Payton's return to play-calling duties. The game will provide an early look at how the Broncos offense performs under Payton's direction.

articles.title: Josh Hart not stressed over Knicks tabling extension talks: ‘Everything is going to work out’
articles.summary: With no deal in place and the Knicks now saying they’ll be tabling contract extension talks until later in the year, Josh Hart isn't stressing.
articles.body:
Josh Hart made it clear in the opening days of training camp that he had hoped him and the Knicks would be able to come to terms on a new contract extension before the start of the season.

With no new deal in place and the team now saying they'll be tabling those discussions until later in the year, though, the dynamic power forward isn't stressing.

"Not looking too much into it," Hart said Saturday. "Obviously we have high expectations, so it's good there we're able to just focus on the season and just keep things moving."

The veteran said that's exactly where his main focus is heading into the year, despite voicing past concerns over his uncertain future serving as a potential distraction.

"At the end of the day I'm still under contract in New York," Hart emphasized. "We have a hell of a team that's trying to repeat, I'm in an amazing situation, so it's not frustrating at all.

"Obviously you want to get some of those things done but if it doesn't, it's nothing where you lose sleep over -- we're blessed to be out here playing basketball for a living, so you just have to block out the noise and keep moving."

Hart is set to earn $20.9 million this season, and he has a team option for next year.

The high-energy do-it-all power forward is expected to play a significant role for New York once again, particularly on the glass with the loss of big man Mitchell Robinson to the Celtics in free agency.

Hart was massive in that area during the Knicks' drought-snapping title run, and he's averaged just over eight rebounds per game during his three-plus years with the team.

articles.title: Nkunku hat-trick powers Leipzig to thumping win over Eintracht Frankfurt
articles.summary: RB Leipzig maintained their perfect home record this season with a clear 6-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday evening.Die Roten Bullen made a blister...
articles.body:
RB Leipzig maintained their perfect home record this season with a clear 6-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday evening.

Die Roten Bullen made a blistering start, racing into a 2-0 lead inside the opening five minutes. Ezechiel Banzuzi opened the scoring within the first minute before Christopher Nkunku doubled Leipzig's advantage, finishing off a well-worked move set up by Antonio Nusa.

After the early setback, Eintracht gradually grew into the contest and threatened to pull a goal back through Ritsu Doan and Ansgar Knauff, but they were both denied by Maarten Vandevoordt, who produced important saves to preserve Leipzig's two-goal cushion.

Leipzig then effectively put the contest beyond doubt before half-time, with Nkunku completing his hat-trick by pouncing on rebounds on two separate occasions to extend the hosts' lead to 4-0 at the break.

The hosts continued where they left off after the restart and added a fifth in the 54th minute. Nusa drove forward with purpose before unleashing a powerful effort that beat Noah Atubolu at his near post.

Leipzig took their foot off the gas a bit after Nusa's goal, withdrawing several key players ahead of a hectic run of fixtures. However, they still had one final goal in them, as second-half substitute Tidiam Gomis burst forward to make it 6-0 and put the finishing touch on a dominant performance just before the final whistle.

The win lifts Martin Demichelis' side to fifth in the Bundesliga table, while Adi Hütter's Eintracht Frankfurt drop to 13th.

articles.title: Nashville Predators' Vitali Pinchuk to make NHL debut vs Ottawa Senators
articles.summary: Vitali Pinchuk, a 24-year-old center out of the KHL, will make his NHL debut for the Nashville Predators against the Ottawa Senators on Oct. 10.
articles.body:
Nashville Predators rookie Vitali Pinchuk will make his NHL debut against the Ottawa Senators on Oct. 10 (6 p.m. CT, The Spot Nashville 28).

The Predators made the announcement shortly after morning skate in Ottawa, while also announcing that defenseman Jayden Struble, who was acquired in a trade with Montreal on Oct. 9 , will make his Predators debut against the Senators.

Pinchuk spent the last four seasons with Dynamo Minsk (KHL) before signing with the Predators on April 27. The 24-year-old was assigned to the AHL before opening night and played one game with the Milwaukee Admirals on Oct. 3. He was recalled from Milwaukee on Oct. 4.

Pinchuk signed a one-year, entry-level contract worth $1 million, choosing Nashville over several other NHL teams. The left-handed center scored 31 goals and 35 assists in 65 games for Dynamo last season.

Nashville Predators open training camp at Ford Ice Center Bellevue

Entering training camp, Pinchuk was a bit of a mystery. A native of Zhlobin, Belarus, Pinchuk played one season with the Kingston Frontenacs (OHL) in 2019-20, but left for the KHL after he was not selected in the 2020 NHL Draft.

Pinchuk played in the Predators' rookie tournament in North Carolina in early September, then played in two preseason games during full camp. Against the Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 24, Pinchuk scored a goal on his first shift, then added an assist in a 6-5 loss.

A 6-foot-3, 203-pound forward, Pinchuk is a smart offensive player with good net-front instincts. His puck skills and shooting seem NHL ready, but his speed and skating are going to need work. He will likely play a minor role on the bottom six while he adjusts to NHL speed.

Struble was acquired for a 2027 second-round pick. The 25-year-old has played 174 games for the Canadiens scoring seven goals and 28 assists. He was originally a second round pick in 2019.

articles.title: Michael Carrick reaction: What did Man United boss say after shambolic start, dramatic draw vs Spurs?
articles.summary: It was a game of two halves — or three periods, as it were — as Manchester United probably deserved their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday, but th...
articles.body:
It was a game of two halves — or three periods, as it were — as Manchester United probably deserved their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday, but the manner in which it occurred will drive Michael Carrick mad the rest of the weekend.

Below is the latest Michael Carrick reaction, speaking after his side were beyond shocking for 60 minutes at Old Trafford, only for Bryan Mbeumo to save the day with a fantastic goal and Rodrigo Bentancur to seal the deal with a headbutt on Luke Shaw a few minutes later. It looked like three points in the bag for Man United, until Dominic Solanke headed home the equalizer in stoppage time.

The result make this Manchester United's worst start to a league campaign for 40 years (12th place, six points).
