articles.title: Top-30 overall recruit Ahmed Nur commits to Ole Miss
articles.summary: Four-star power forward Ahmed Nur has committed to Ole Miss, he told Rivals. The 6-foot-8 senior out of Bella Vista Prep (AZ) chose the Rebels over Florida S...
articles.body:
Four-star power forward Ahmed Nur has committed to Ole Miss , he told Rivals.

The 6-foot-8 senior out of Bella Vista Prep (AZ) chose the Rebels over Florida State, Syracuse, and SMU.

Nur, a native of Hopkins, Minnesota, is ranked as the No. 28 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 4 ranked power forward, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports).

Ahmed Nur discussed his decision to play for Chris Beard and Ole Miss with Rivals.

"I believe I can come in right away and impact winning as a freshman, with a coaching staff that believes I can is very special.

"My relationship was close with coach Beard and we got to know each other well over the visit and stayed connected."

In his own words, what type of player is Ole Miss getting in Ahmed Nur?

"I would say I am a versatile wing. I can do multiple things on the court that impacts winning at a high level."

"Rebel Nation, I'm excited for what's ahead. I'm ready to get to work, represent Ole Miss the right way, and give y'all something to be proud of. Hotty Toddy!"

Rivals National Recruiting Analyst Jamie Shaw found Nur to be one of the top performers at the Overtime Elite Pro Day a couple weeks ago, writing this about him:

Ahmed Nur is an intriguing prospect. He stands out immediately with legit size with athletic fluidity and a smooth shooting stroke when given time. His flashes are very intriguing. He was able to get on the rim a couple times in the small-sided games and he knocked down a few pull-up jump shots. Finding consistency in performance will be next with him, getting stronger and playing off a steady base. There is an intriguing long-term possibility here.

articles.title: Martinez to blame for Tottenham’s goal but this United flop was a walking disaster in gut-wrenching 1-1 draw: Player Ratings
articles.summary: Manchester United were held to a 1-1 draw by Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford. Here are our player ratings from the game.(A score of 6 is around average)Sen...
articles.body:
Manchester United were held to a 1-1 draw by Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford. Here are our player ratings from the game.

Senne Lammens 5 – Shaky display. Nervy from the off, he gifted the ball to a Tottenham player and never looked comfortable in possession.

Leny Yoro 7 – Solid. He was one of the few United players to deliver a strong performance throughout his time on the pitch, producing several exceptional tackles, impressing on the ball and matching Savinho. A positive outing after a dream international break.

Harry Maguire 5 – OK. Nothing to rave about.

Lisandro Martinez 4 – Outmuscled by Dominic Solanke for Tottenham's equaliser. Not good enough.

Luke Shaw 6 – Decent defensively. He advanced when the opportunity presented itself, providing the overlap and seeking to deliver crosses into the box.

Kobbie Mainoo 6 – He was dispossessed several times, though to be fair to him, he was overburdened defensively as a result of insufficient support from his midfield colleagues. He improved as the match developed.

Youri Tielemans 2 – Dreadful. Repeatedly dispossessed, offering negligible to no defensive output, and he undoubtedly remained on the field longer than was warranted.

Bruno Fernandes 3 – Also poor. Such was his inadequacy on the ball in the first half that one might be forgiven for doubting he was a footballer. His decision-making was poor, and he proved more of a liability than anything else.

Amad 4 – Endured a laboured evening on his return from injury.

Matheus Cunha 6 – He battled and was heavily involved, although little was coming off for him until he registered the assist.

Bryan Mbeumo 8 – Excellent finish to give United the lead.

Carlos Baleba 7.5 – United were toiling in midfield until he came on and changed everything; energy, defensive solidity, quality on the ball. A brilliant debut, spoiled only by the lost three points.

Joshua Zirkzee 6 – Some nice touches and turns as United chased the three points.

Marcus Rashford 5 – On for in added time.

articles.title: Kansas State vs Houston: 2026 Game 5
articles.summary: The Wildcats are back at home looking to get back on track.
articles.body:
Following an off week to regroup, your Kansas State Wildcats return to the friendly confines of Bill Snyder Family Stadium looking to get back on track after a lackluster performance in the Big 12 opener at Cincinnati led to a 26-31 loss to the Bearcats.

So now, back in Manhattan, the Wildcats will look back in gear. But it won't be easy, as the Willie Fritz-led Houston Cougars are in town also looking to avoid their second loss of the season. Fritz is no stranger to success in Manhattan, as he was the head man at Tulane when the Green Wave shocked the Wildcats in 2022. Then in 2024 down in Houston, his Cougars squad knocked off K-State 24-19. No matter the team or situation, Fritz seems to have figured out the Wildcats.

Of course, the K-State head coach in both those games was the now-retired Chris Klieman. The K-State faithful have to hope that Collin Klein's leadership can lead them to finally beating Willie Fritz. But it won't be easy. K-State was exposed against the Bearcats on both sides of the ball, the kind of things that we only had glimpses of against Wazzu and Tulane. But against a Big 12 team, the Cats talent advantage was mostly negated. And it will be the same today against Houston, a Cougars squad that went toe-to-toe with the Fighting Mercs Red Raiders in Lubbock and came up a yard short of knocking off the defending champs.

K-State has what it takes to win this game, but it's going to take a big step up in effort, focus, and execution if the Wildcats want to pick up their first Big 12 win in 2026.

We've got an 2:30pm CT kickoff from Bill Snyder Family Stadium being aired on FOX with Tim Brando (play-by-play), Devin Gardner (analyst), and Josh Sims (sidelines) on the call.

If you don't have FOX or can't access the stream, the game can be heard across the 29-station K-State Sports Network with Wyatt Thompson (play-by-play), former K-State quarterback Stan Weber (analysis), and Matt Walters (sidelines) calling the action. The game will also be on SiriusXM Satellite Radio Ch. 173 or 237, and available online via the Varsity Network app . Live stats are also available at k-statesports.com, and Twitter updates (@KStateFB) will also be a part of the coverage.

articles.title: Kentucky gets a surprise visit from 2027 center
articles.summary: Mark Pope and the Kentucky basketball team received a surprise visit from one of the top centers in the 2027 class on Friday.
articles.body:
Kentucky basketball coach Mark Pope is on a mission to prove that he can recruit, and land, elite recruits this offseason. Last year's chase of Tyran Stokes likely cost him other recruits, and they learned a lesson. This year, they already have a commitment from four-star forward Ryan Hampton, and they are working on many others in the 2027 class, including center Cherif Millogo .

Millogo is a rising star in the class who Kentucky offered back in May, and have prioritized. It may be paying off. On Friday, the coveted center made a trip to Lexington for a surprise official visit, as reported by Jack Pilgrim of Kentucky Sports Radio.

Standing at 7'5", 240 lbs, Millogo has impressive and unteachable size. He is currently rated four stars by 247Sports and ranks as their No. 44 overall player. Some services have him ranked even higher, and he's moving up.

Kentucky has some tough competition for Millogo's services. Arkansas, Kansas, Louisville, and multiple SEC teams are also in contention. Getting him in for a visit is certainly a win for the Wildcats, but having him choose to make a surprise visit is a good sign.

articles.title: Aces face an offseason shake-up after semifinal sweep, with Jackie Young's future looming
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Anything short of a WNBA championship is considered a disappointment for the Aces, so changes almost certainly are coming after Las Vegas wa...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — Anything short of a WNBA championship is considered a disappointment for the Aces , so changes almost certainly are coming after Las Vegas was swept out of the semifinals by Golden State on Friday night.

Whether that change involves the Big Three is the Aces' biggest question entering the offseason because five-time All-Star guard Jackie Young is a free agent.

She averaged career highs in points per game (18.9) and assists (6.8) to go with a 4.4-rebounding average and shooting percentages of 48.8 from the floor and 38.3 from 3-point range.

"I think she had a career year this year," coach Becky Hammon said. "Had some unbelievable performances throughout the season, so obviously it's a big priority that we retain her services. We'll see what those thoughts look like, but I know what it looks like from our end. Ultimately, it's going to come down to her decision."

If Young returns, she will rejoin a core that includes five-time MVP A'ja Wilson and six-time All-Star point guard Chelsea Gray that has been instrumental in winning three of the past four titles.

While Wilson clearly wants Young to return, she also wants to be mindful of not being overbearing while trying to persuade her to re-sign.

"I'm constantly in Jackie's ear," Wilson said. "I know when she needs that big sister, but also when she needs that space. So going into this offseason, I'm just going to be me. I'm not going change too much because that's not what Jackie needs."

If Young leaves, the Aces could be aggressive in going after a big-name free agent such as Indiana's Kelsey Mitchell or Minnesota's Napheesa Collier.

Mitchell expressed frustration a week ago about playing in the glare that comes with having Caitlin Clark as a teammate. Clark made the case on Thursday for keeping Mitchell , which would again give the Fever one of the league's top backcourts.

Even if Young comes back, that doesn't mean the Aces will sit still.

"We're going to make some adjustments, we're going to make some moves, try to address our weaknesses," Hammon said shortly after Friday night's 87-77 overtime loss to the Valkyries. "That's not a question to answer right now. There's a lot of things coming through my head."

Top of mind was not having a good enough defense, and that likely will be a top priority for Hammon and team president and general manager Nikki Fargas. Hammon said the lack of an elite defense is a major reason the Aces are already into their offseason.

But it's not so simple to improve just one area.

Hammon lamented injuries that ended NaLyssa Smith's season and limited Jewell Loyd, Stephanie Talbot and Dana Evans.

"This is why repeating is hard," she said. "There has to be some things that go your way. You have to get some lucky breaks, and we've been pretty lucky around here. We've done some good things and made our own breaks at times. Other times, it's tougher to make those little things happen for you. And there's some things that happen that are completely out of your control."
